findings.title: MCP list/search calls add batched SLA tracker reads on core GraphQL
findings.failure: Every getThreads (default first: 10) and searchThreads (default first: 50) invocation now resolves serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary per thread, which batches to getLatestServiceLevelAgreementTrackersByThreadIdsUnsafe against service_level_agreement_trackers. Under heavy MCP traffic this adds DB read load and response size on core-graphql-api compared to HEAD~1, which could contribute to latency or timeouts on the 25s WEB lambda / 30s API Gateway cap.
findings.fix: Monitor core-graphql-api latency and DB load after MCP deploy; if hot, consider narrowing default selections, lowering searchThreads page size in tool docs, or a product decision to omit summary on high-volume list tools.
findings.evidence: HEAD~1 operations omitted serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary; resolver calls serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader when tierId or serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId is set (packages/core-graphql/src/resolvers.ts ~7761–7776); dataloader uses DISTINCT ON latest trackers query (serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDb.ts ~151–155). searchThreads still defaults first: 50.

findings.title: SLA filter matches any historical tracker row; summary is newest per type
findings.failure: An agent filtering slaStatuses: [BREACHED] can receive threads whose serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary shows PENDING (or another status) on a target, because EXISTS matches any tracker row while summary uses latest created_at per (thread_id, type). Agents may mis-rank urgency or give wrong answers despite technically correct API behavior.
findings.fix: No code change required if intentional; ensure tool descriptions stay prominent (already partially documented). Optionally add a short example in getThreads comments showing summary vs filter divergence.
findings.evidence: Filter uses EXISTS on service_level_agreement_trackers without “latest only” (threadDbFilterUtils.ts). Summary uses getLatestServiceLevelAgreementTrackersByThreadIds with ORDER BY created_at DESC DISTINCT ON type (serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDb.ts). PR summary.md and getThreads.graphql header describe the same caveat.

findings.title: searchThreads exposes SLA summary but not SLA filters
findings.failure: Agents using searchThreads for text search cannot narrow by slaStatuses/slaTypes (only getThreads can). Workflows like “search title X and show breaching SLAs” require a two-step getThreads filter or accept unfiltered SLA noise in search results.
findings.fix: If product wants parity, add optional slaStatuses/slaTypes variables to searchThreads filters the same way as getThreads; otherwise document in searchThreads header that SLA filtering requires getThreads.
findings.evidence: diff.patch adds serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary to searchThreads only; getThreads.graphql adds $slaStatuses/$slaTypes and filters.serviceLevelAgreements. Grep serviceLevelAgreements under services/mcp-server/operations hits only getThreads.graphql.

findings.title: Duplicate SLA status selection set (~180 lines × 3 files)
findings.failure: Future field additions (e.g. new status detail fields) require three identical edits; one missed file causes MCP tools to return inconsistent SLA shapes across tools.
findings.fix: Add a shared GraphQL fragment file under services/mcp-server/operations/ (validateMcpOperations.ts merges all .graphql definitions into one document) mirroring lambdas/agent-sandbox-api/src/proxy/services/plain/fragments.ts SLA_FRAGMENT pattern, extended to firstResolutionTime and totalResolutionTime.
findings.evidence: diff.patch repeats the same serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary selection in three operations. Grep for fragment in services/mcp-server: no matches. agent-sandbox-api already centralizes SLA_FRAGMENT in fragments.ts.

checked_fine: Deploy: diff touches only services/mcp-server/operations/*.graphql; Dockerfile copies operations into image; no migrations, SST/OpenTofu resource, env var, or permission changes in diff.

Contract: additive GraphQL selections and optional getThreads variables; routes/auth unchanged; core schema already defines serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary and ServiceLevelAgreementFilter (packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts).

Default getThreads SLA filters: inline serviceLevelAgreements { statuses: null, types: null } does not add SQL when both are null (threadDbFilterUtils.ts inner guard at types/statuses/updatedAt); parity with omitting filter when variables unset.
Contract validation: lint:mcpGraphql runs validateMcpOperations.ts against @team-plain/core-graphql schema (package.json lint script).
Data / rollback: no stored schema or migration changes; rolling back MCP image restores prior tool responses only (one-way door none).
Blast radius: no shared TS constants or aggregate changes in diff; behavior change limited to MCP operation documents.

Resolver parity: serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary uses existing dataloader and union resolvers (resolvers.ts ~7761–7776, ~9433–9457); threads without tier and policy return all-null without DB load.
Dead code: repo search for serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary under services/mcp-server shows three operation usages only; no new unreachable exports in diff.
Silent regression (deploy triggers): mcp-server ECS image rebuild picks up operation file changes via fromAsset(services/mcp-server).
Operability (core API): no duplicated infra values introduced by this PR.
